experiments.evidence: Own same-page A/B: shipped GLBs against ORM bytes from ac10d5386^, swapped on every fighter on the field, same held frame, new seeds and moments. Frames: _harness/_shots/gfx_verify_GF/{rift_high_s83,rift_ultra_s97,bridge_high_s61,fray_high_s37,rift_low_s83}, each with report.json; solo: _harness/_shots/gfx_verify_solo_{vashil,ulkro,burdam}_*. Teamfight frames at 28.5 m and at the real default 31 m, actual size, not zoomed: I could not tell before from after, on High or Ultra. Pixels changed by more than 8: 293-992 of 2.07M per frame (0.014-0.048 %), and 84-278 on solo frames. Largest fighter delta is Marund (dome, top-quartile L* +2 at most); other fighters mean dL +0.5 to +2 on changed pixels. Low: fighter pixels unchanged (burst and pan metrics identical), so Low gets no benefit and no extra weight. Collection stage, all 48 GLBs (16 bases and the 32 skins the engineer did not inspect; _harness/_shots/gfx_verify_GF/stage): a real but mixed change. Hesmi, Ardit and Nurrow's hat gain some material separation. Vashil's robe picks up brown streaks on all 3 of its GLBs, worst on vashil_first_bell and vashil_chalkline (16234 px >8, 3705 >24), and Marund and Nurrow cloth also reads grimier. The claim 'matte cloth unchanged' does not hold for fighters whose cloth sits in the sheen classes: Vashil's roughness p90 goes 0.824 to 0.60, median 0.651 to 0.384. A lossless grade (_harness/_shots/gfx_verify_GF/stage_ll) shows the same streaks by eye, so the curve causes them, not the encoder (visual only: that run is a different page and pose). No budget break: triangles, draws and programs identical in every A/B (programs 39 rift, 38 bridge, 30 fray, 27 Low); ORM dimensions identical on 48 of 48, so texture memory is unchanged by construction, not measured as an A/B. Timing A/B was at load 11-29 and block noise exceeds any delta: not_measured. value_probe on the graded tree (rift, bridge High, _harness/_reports/gfx_verify_GF_value.json): 30 PASS, 0 FAIL, laneP50 89, fighterTop25 80.5 against 80.3 in the committed report. Shimmer: no clear change. Frozen-sim pan flick +0.02 to +0.08 of about 10 on fighter boxes, always up but within about 0.7 %; on changed pixels over consecutive frames, up on rift High (53.1 to 56.7), down on bridge and Ultra, flat on fray. Telegraphs: unchanged to the eye; pixels changed outside fighter boxes are 0-152 on High and Ultra, at the level of the same-frame control noise, and Low's 727 is on a page whose fighters did not change. Team and hue: mean da and db within about 1.4 on changed pixels. Sensitivity: no mask or face changed its reading on any of the 48. With the same fps and memory there is no runtime cost, but the cost is not zero: every rebuild silently drops the grade, so it needs a new closing-gate row and a post-build step, and the Vashil robes get worse. The gain at the game camera, the bar of this pass, is too small for a player to see.
experiments.fixHint: git revert ac10d5386 (no later commit touches art/out/fighters), then npm run content, and drop the closing-gate and post-build handoffs. Keep the rejected A/B sheet as the record. If the lead wants a Collection-only polish later: exempt the cloth parts (a roughness curve cannot tell robe cloth from lacquer at 0.65, so use the part map), and re-judge Vashil and Marund first.

regressions: Collection stage: brown streaks on Vashil's robe from the roughness curve, worst on vashil_first_bell and vashil_chalkline (_harness/_shots/gfx_verify_GF/stage/vashil_first_bell_{pre,post}.png). Not a sensitivity call, a quality loss on paid skins.

Claim wrong, 'sets metal to 0': the lossy re-encode brings it back. Decoded B on the 16 bases, max 0.17-0.34, p99 0.04-0.18, down from max 0.23-0.55, and materials with the default metallicFactor do read it. Reduced, not zero; Nurrow's p99 did not drop (0.122 both) and its max rose (0.227 to 0.282).

Second-generation lossy encode moves AO inside islands: mean absolute 0.011-0.042 and p99 up to 0.153 on the 256 px ORMs (Ulkro, Ervet, Kemdo). High-frequency roughness rises on Lisvel (0.025 to 0.045) and Nurrow (0.035 to 0.039). Scratchpad audit, reproducible from ac10d5386^ against HEAD.
Nurrow facing 90 bottom band at 36.0 against the 35 ceiling is the engineer's Cycles reading, not re-run here; a revert removes it.
summary: Fail as delivered: revert GF-1. At the game camera in busy teamfights on rift, bridge and fray, High and Ultra, 28.5 m and 31 m, it changes 0.014-0.048 % of the frame and I could not see it. Low is unaffected. In Collection the gain is real but mixed: some fighters separate better, while Vashil's robes get streakier. Triangles, draws and programs are identical and value_probe passes, so nothing breaks a budget, but the grade adds a rebuild trap for no gain a player can see in play. GF-2 and GF-3 are correctly rejected. The engineer's game-camera crops on his sheet are upscaled, and even there the difference is hard to find. All timing was at load 11-29, so it is not_measured, and match memory was not measured as an A/B. Nothing was fixed; the revert is the lead's.
